text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SLO breach detected for router tail latency (p99 > 1.5s) in eu-west-2. Severity: P2. Alert: router.tail.p99 > 1.5s for 3m. page: @oncall-alex @sre-lina

oncall-alex: saw it, joining bridge now. can everyone post quick checks (ingress rates, LB errors, recent deploys)?

sre-lina: looking at dashboards — p95 jumped ~400ms, p99 up to 2.1s. Streaming stalls showing increased reconnects. Ingress QPS stable, error rate not spiked.

eng-runtime-miguel: no runtime deploys in last 30m. I see increased queue latency on a subset of router pods in eu-west-2, tail CPU spikes on node group rg-router-12.

eng-router-sara: we rolled a routing-weight tweak 12m ago (policy rollout: prefer-local=0.6 -> 0.8) to prefer local zones. Could be related. Rolling back in progress?

oncall-alex: @eng-router-sara please confirm exact change id if available. If it correlates, rollback and pin previous policy.

eng-router-sara: change id: rollout/2026-03-15-preferlocal-42. Started at 1758003600. I'm seeing hot partitioning: particular shard bucket A47 is getting 8x more binds on a few balancers. Likely LB weight skew + prefer-local push.

support-jordan: we've got two customer tickets reporting slower streaming responses since ~10:10 UTC. No errors, just stalls. Customers affected: beta-corp, retail-prod.

product-evan: estimating customer-impact window — can we get p99 by customer/tenant? need quick impact note for CS.

ops-jen: oncall infra — launching a small canary to redirect 5% of traffic to alternative balancer set in eu-west-2. Command: `infractl route set --region eu-west-2 --set override_group=balancer-b`

eng-runtime-miguel: added KV-cache warmup for balancer-b, starting canary. Observing one canary shard reply times down by ~30% already.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://call.redwood/incident/1758004321 - oncall: @oncall-alex

sre-lina: telemetry: overlayed per-shard p99. Bucket A47 p99 = 3.4s, others ~0.9s. Topology map shows A47 pinned to nodes in az-2 that have stale routing table entries.

eng-router-sara: digging — looks like a seed update failed to propagate to a subset of routers (seed-sync error 502). Those routers kept old sticky mappings causing hotkey fan-in to same nodes. This + prefer-local weight amplification == hot partition.

eng-runtime-miguel: can confirm `seed-sync` logs: `ERROR sync: remote 10.2.88.7 timeout` from router pod rtr-az2-17. Network ACLs look fine. Possibly transient control-plane lag during rollout.

oncall-alex: mitigation plan: 1) pause prefer-local rollout (stop rollout controller), 2) force re-seed sync to affected routers, 3) shift 20% traffic to balancer-b as temporary spread, 4) monitor p99 and streaming reconnects. Who owns 2?

eng-router-sara: I'll take 1 & 2. Running `kubectl annotate rollout/rollout-42 pause=true` then `routerctl reseed --target pods rtr-az2-* --force`

ops-jen: I'll continue traffic steering (3). Starting script now.

support-jordan: sending heads-up to CS: impacted tenants list + we will update in 15m.

customer-success-amy: thanks — will brief customers and collect any live logs. Please flag any change in visible latency per tenant.

(2m later)

eng-router-sara: paused rollout. forced reseed returned success for 9/12 pods; 3 still flaky — restarting those pods now. Logs show earlier seed blob mismatch.

eng-runtime-miguel: after restart, rtr-az2-17 seed-sync healthy. CPU tail normalized on restarted nodes.

ops-jen: reroute completed: 20% -> balancer-b. Canary metrics: canary p99=0.78s, main group p99 dropped to 1.1s from 2.1s. Streaming reconnects down 65%.

sre-lina: good signal. p99 trending down. p95 back to baseline. Recording SLO window and start of mitigation for postmortem timeline.

oncall-alex: keep measuring for 20m. If stable, we can mark incident mitigated and keep a follow-up action: root cause remediation + safer rollout gating.

product-evan: capturing impact numbers: approx 4% requests in eu-west-2 hit p99 > 1.5s for a 12m window. Affected customers flagged.

support-jordan: notified customers with summary and ETA for deeper RCA. No escalations.

eng-router-sara: root cause notes for RCA: 1) rollout increased preferential weight causing concentration, 2) seed-sync propagation failed for subset of az routers (control-plane retry/backoff issue), 3) router sticky mapping amplified hotkey effects. Immediate fix: add rollout canary step to validate seed-sync status before increasing weights; add rollout gating on per-shard heatmap.

eng-runtime-miguel: engineering follow-ups: enhance `routerctl reseed` to auto-retry with exponential backoff and alert if >10% pods fail reseed within 2m. Also add health check that flags sticky-map skew.

sre-lina: action items: SLO impact window: 1758003600-1758004320 (12m). Postmortem lead: @eng-router-sara. Oncall follow-up: @oncall-alex to verify rollback playbook.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P3 — monitoring.

oncall-alex: marking mitigated for now. Will keep thread open for RCA drafts. Thanks all for fast coordination. :thumbsup:

customer-success-amy: customers updated, no further reports.

(After 40m)

eng-router-sara: starting postmortem draft: will include timeline, dashboards, logs and checklist for rollout policy changes. Tagging @product-evan for decisions around prefer-local defaults.

product-evan: let's discuss safe defaults and rollout guardrails tomorrow. Add discussion item: should prefer-local be lower by default for small shards?

support-jordan: closing customer tickets with incident reference.

sre-lina: adding incident notes to ops-runbook and scheduling a follow-up retro.

oncall-alex: closing bridge in 10. If anything new, re-open thread. Great job everyone.
